title: Layered rotating circulation and its vorticity hotspots
query: Using the supplied CMOMS daily velocity, temperature and salinity for 2011-2020, test the following findings of Gan et al. (2022, Nature Communications, doi:10.1038/s41467-022-29610-z) for the South China Sea basin: (1) the basin-scale circulation rotates in alternating directions in vertically stacked layers, cyclonic in the upper layer, anticyclonic in the middle layer and cyclonic in the deep layer; (2) in each layer the circulation, identified through Stokes' theorem as the area integral of relative vorticity over the basin, is dominated by a few energetic hotspots with large vorticity whose contribution far exceeds their share of the area; (3) these hotspots also supply most of the energy needed to form and maintain the rotating circulation. Give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain any differences from the paper.

paper.title: Hotspots of the stokes rotating circulation in a large marginal sea
